The Lord addresses Moses about the lamps: Aaron places seven lamps, whose light faces the front from one side. The directional expression is retained without an invented diagram of the fixture.
Aaron lights the lamps from the one side toward the front, following the instruction. The explicit one belongs to this verse.
Solid gold, stem and lilies describe the whole lampstand; its form follows the divine showing. The implicit maker remains unnamed.
A new divine speech introduces Levitical purification.
Levites are taken from among Israel and purified; separation and cleansing are distinct actions.
Sprinkling, shaving the whole body and washing garments precede cleanness. No water recipe is added here.
They take the first calf and flour offering, while you take the year-old sin calf. The selected shift in agent and the second calf's explicit age remain.
Levites are brought before the tent and the whole congregation is assembled.
Israel's sons lay hands upon the Levites before the Lord. The action is not assigned to Aaron alone.
Aaron separates the Levites as Israel's gift before the Lord for the Lord's work. No physical waving of the men is asserted.
Levites lay hands on the calves; the singular he then offers them for sin and whole burning. The unnamed offering agent is not replaced by a new name.
The selected text includes before the Lord as well as before Aaron and his sons. All three placements remain.
Separation from Israel establishes divine possession, expressed as Mine.
Entry into tent work is followed in the wording by cleansing and giving before the Lord. The sequence is not rearranged to remove repetition.
Given as a gift represents the repeated gift language; all womb-opening firstborn are the group replaced.
Both human and livestock firstborn belong to God, with Egypt's striking and consecration tied to the same day.
Levites replace every firstborn among Israel. The repeated substitution statement remains.
The gift to Aaron serves Israel's work and atonement. The selected ending excludes anyone approaching the holy things; it does not mention a plague.
Moses, Aaron and the whole congregation obey concerning the Levites. Everything renders the comprehensive as-commanded relation, not an extra ritual action.
Levites purify themselves and wash clothes; Aaron presents them and makes atonement to purify them. The agents remain distinct.
Levitical ministry begins afterward before Aaron and his sons. The closing obedience formula remains.
A fresh divine speech introduces service ages.
Service starts at twenty-five and upward in the selected text. No thirty-year threshold is imported.
At fifty the individual withdraws and no longer works. The change from plural to singular is retained.
His brother is the explicit ministering subject in the selected Greek. The subsequent no-work clause remains without replacing brother with an interpretation.
column3: The referent of the implicit subject in the no-work clause requires syntactic review.

The Lord addresses Moses about the lamps: The date is first month of the second year after departure from Egypt, in Sinai. It is not changed to match the earlier census date.
Moses must tell Israel to observe Passover at its appointed time.
Fourteenth day, first month and evening are all explicit. Law and prescribed determination remain distinct terms.
column3: The best natural equivalent of the final regulatory noun remains open for lexical review.

The Lord addresses Moses about the lamps: Moses transmits the command to observe Passover.
The unusual opening participle and fourteenth-day date remain without adding first month or evening from verse 3.
column3: At the beginning is provisional for the compressed participial opening; its construction needs further review.

The Lord addresses Moses about the lamps: Corpse-unclean men cannot observe on that day and approach both Moses and Aaron. The repeated that day remains.
The men's question challenges being deprived of presenting the gift because of impurity. Must we preserves its negative rhetorical expectation.
Moses tells them to remain while he hears the Lord's command concerning them. He does not invent a ruling himself.
Divine speech supplies the answer to the petition.
Corpse impurity and a distant journey are alternative qualifying conditions, applying now and in later generations.
The deferred observance is evening of the fourteenth day of the second month, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
Leaving any until morning and breaking a bone are both prohibited. The general Passover-law clause remains.
Cleanliness, no distant journey and failure to observe jointly define the sanction. Destruction from the people and bearing sin are both retained.
Sojourner and native share one law. The selected text explicitly locates the sojourner in your land.
The cloud covers the erected tent, called the House of Testimony; an appearance like fire remains until morning.
Continual cloud by day and fire appearance by night are both preserved, without turning appearance into a material description.
The cloud's rising governs departure and its standing governs the camping place. Israel's sons are named in both actions.
The source places camping before departure and repeats the command formula; all cloud-shadowed days are spent camped.
A prolonged stay requires keeping God's charge and emphatically not setting out. The negative is retained.
A number of days remains unspecified. Voice governs camping and command governs departure, retaining the selected lexical distinction.
Evening-to-morning presence and morning rising precede the day-or-night departure expression. The compact sequence is not harmonized to a fuller alternative.
The selected month-days expression is retained without importing two days or a year. Continued cloud cover prohibits departure.
column3: The compressed duration syntax merits further review before final acceptance.

The Lord addresses Moses about the lamps: Departure by command and the retrospectively kept charge remain; through Moses naturally renders mediation by his hand.
The Lord's speech opens the trumpet instructions.
Two silver trumpets are hammered work, for assembling the congregation and moving the camps. Both purposes remain.
Blowing both gathers the whole congregation at the tent door.
One trumpet gathers all rulers, identified as Israel's leaders. The selected plural they blow remains.
A signal first moves the eastern camps; no duration or musical pitch is invented.
Second, third and fourth signals and all their directional camps are explicit in the selected text and retained. Sea remains the western directional image.
column3: Southwest for the second direction follows the provisional rendering in 2:10; its contextual directional range remains open.

The Lord addresses Moses about the lamps: Ordinary assembly blowing is distinguished from the departure signal. The negation remains explicit.
Aaron's priestly sons are the trumpeters, under an enduring statute for the generations.
War in their land against resisting enemies calls for a trumpet signal, remembrance before the Lord and deliverance. No extra divine title is inserted.
Glad days, festivals and new moons are all included, over whole burnt and deliverance offerings. Remembrance and the divine self-identification close the command.
The cloud rises on day twenty of month two in year two. All three date components remain.
Israel travels with equipment in Sinai and the cloud stands in Paran. Equipment follows the selected noun, not an imported stage-by-stage itinerary.
First and the Lord's voice through Moses remain in the brief departure statement.
Judah's formation leaves first, with Nahshon son of Amminadab over its army.
Issachar's army is under Nethanel son of Zuar, following Judah.
Zebulun's army is under Eliab son of Helon, completing the first group.
The text shifts to future instructions: dismantling and Gershon and Merari carrying the tent. The shift is retained.
Reuben's formation departs with Elizur son of Shedeur over its army.
Simeon's army is under Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
Gad's army is under Eliasaph son of Reuel. The selected father-name is not harmonized to Deuel.
Kohath carries the holy things; tent erection precedes their arrival. Both clauses remain.
column3: The two implicit they subjects can be confused in English; a fuller discourse review must decide how to distinguish the tent carriers from the arriving Kohathites without adding unsupported agency.

The Lord addresses Moses about the lamps: Ephraim's formation follows, with Elishama son of Ammihud over its army; the selected future is retained.
Manasseh's army is under Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
Benjamin's army is under Abidan son of Gideoni.
Dan's formation is last of all camps, under Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai. Last is not expanded into an unexpressed military duty.
Asher's army is under Pagiel son of Ocran.
Naphtali's army is under Ahira son of Enan, completing the list.
The summary identifies Israel's armies and their departure with their force, retaining both collective nouns.
Moses invites the named Midianite relative to the promised place and promises good. Kinsman by marriage avoids over-specifying the relationship.
column3: Hobab is an inherited conventional equivalent for the selected Greek Iobab; its approval remains open in the name register.

The Lord addresses Moses about the lamps: The response refuses the proposed journey in favour of his land and kin. The English supplies go in the contrasting clause from the expressed motion verb.
Moses appeals to the man's wilderness companionship and future role as elder. The selected elder is not replaced by eyes or guide.
The promised benefit is conditional on accompanying them and connected to the good the Lord does for Israel.
Both three-day journey expressions remain, with the ark going ahead to seek rest. No alternative marching position is imposed.
Moses invokes the Lord at departure; scattering enemies and fleeing haters retain all. Thine and Thee correctly address God.
The rest invocation retains the selected transitive-looking turn-back expression with thousands and myriads in Israel.
column3: The relation of the accusative numbers to the imperative needs syntactic and apparatus review; no familiar unto reading is substituted.

The Lord addresses Moses about the lamps: The cloud-shading statement follows the two invocations in this selected order. Its day-time setting and departure from camp remain.
